svg.title: Correct fire perimeters backward, then reveal new growth forward
svg.desc: Three irregular fire perimeters remain visible across the top. Blue copies slide down into the backward row before the backward pass begins. A translucent copy of the latest perimeter then slides onto the middle one. Ground outside that copy turns rose and dissolves. The corrected middle footprint then slides onto the earliest one and trims it in the same way. Copies of all three corrected footprints slide down into the forward row, changing from blue to gold. Then copies slide diagonally from the complete corrected footprints above onto the next footprint and dissolve already counted ground. Three disjoint amber growth regions remain. Static and reduced-motion views show original, corrected and difference geometry together; hatching identifies the retracted original ground.
svg.text: Correct the past, then isolate new growth
The moving copy aligns the same ground in different observations.
Hatching marks ground that later evidence retracts.
Keep only ground shared with the corrected next observation.
Subtract the full corrected predecessor; the remainder is new ground.
The amber regions are disjoint; together they cover the latest perimeter.
Illustrative perimeters. Static / reduced motion shows all three stages.
